title: Counting the Refusals Left Uncured on a Granite Ridge Pass Account
content:
On a Granite Ridge Season Pass Programme pass account, the refusals left uncured past their grace period are counted as late fees raised on that account, and the window over which they are counted is fixed as follows.

**First.** Where the pass record no longer admits the holder, the refusals left uncured are counted as every late fee raised on the pass account since the plan was opened.

**Second.** Where the pass record still admits the holder and the pass account carries a refusal in the three whole months ending on the handling date, the refusals left uncured are counted as the late fees raised in the three whole months ending on the handling date.

**Otherwise.** In any other case the window is not widened by this rule.

### The windows set against the state of the record

| The pass record | Refusals in the three whole months ending on the handling date | Window over which the late fees are counted |
| --- | --- | --- |
| no longer admits the holder | any number, including none | every late fee since the plan was opened |
| still admits the holder | at least 1 | the three whole months ending on the handling date |
| still admits the holder | none | not widened by this rule |

The state of the pass record is read first: while the record no longer admits the holder the window runs back to the opening of the plan whatever the refusals in the shorter window show.

### Worked on a hypothetical account

A pass account whose plan was opened in October carries late fees of 25.00 in November, 25.00 in January and 25.00 in the one whole month ending on a handling date in March.

Where the record no longer admits the holder, all three are counted, giving 3. Where the record still admits the holder and one refusal stands in the three whole months ending in March, the January and March fees are counted, giving 2. Where the record still admits the holder and no refusal stands in that window, this rule does not widen the count.
